articles.title: Energy sector at a crossroads
articles.summary: PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s promotion of nuclear power, waste-to-energy, and more natural gas in his 2026 State of the Nation Address (SONA) was strongly criticized by Greenpeace Southeast Asia-Philippines and other environmental organizations. These energy sources are “costly and hazardous false solutions that deepen Filipinos’ exposure to volatile global markets, health hazards, and environmental degradation,” Greenpeace said in an official statement. Rather, the Philippines should invest “in local solar, wind and modern renewable infrastructure [that] shields consumers from unpredictable global fuel prices, generates sustainable green jobs, and builds a truly resilient economy from the ground up.”

articles.title: Petrol in Delhi would have cost around ₹125/litre without ethanol blending during crude spike, says Centre
articles.titleEn: Petrol in Delhi would have cost around ₹125/litre without ethanol blending during crude spike, says Centre
articles.summary: Petrol in Delhi would have cost around ₹125 per litre when global crude prices hit $135 a barrel, had ethanol not been blended into fuel, the Centre said. Defending the E20 programme, it said consumers instead paid ₹94.77 per litre, calling ethanol India's energy insurance against oil shocks.

articles.title: Mideast war supercharges electric car sales: IEA
articles.titleEn: Mideast war supercharges electric car sales: IEA
articles.summary: Soaring fuel prices due to the Mideast war have supercharged sales of electric cars in the second quarter, the International Energy Agency said Thursday. "Despite a challenging backdrop for the global car market, sales of electric cars surged in the second quarter of this year as the energy crisis sparked by the war in the Middle East brought fuel price volatility back into sharp focus," it said.

articles.title: Global Market: Japan's core inflation picks up in June; BOJ rate outlook keeps markets on edge
articles.titleEn: Global Market: Japan's core inflation picks up in June; BOJ rate outlook keeps markets on edge
articles.summary: Japan's core consumer inflation rose to 1.6% in June. This increase occurred while food prices eased and service inflation slowed. Underlying inflation, excluding food and fuel, also saw a slight decrease. Economists anticipate stronger inflationary pressures later this year due to rising energy costs. The Bank of Japan will consider these figures at its upcoming policy meeting.

articles.title: Crude Nears $100 As Houthi Strikes Fuel Supply Disruption Concerns
